steps.text: Whisk canola oil, sugar, red wine vinegar, and soy sauce together in a large bowl until sugar has dissolved. Toss in cabbage, green onions, almonds, and sunflower seeds. Cover bowl and refrigerate before serving, at least 1 hour; slaw tastes better when chilled overnight.

raw_recipe.headline: Mayo Free Cabbage Salad
raw_recipe.description: This mayo-free cabbage salad recipe is a simple coleslaw that marinates a bag of shredded cabbage in a sweet and tangy dressing and is served cold.
raw_recipe.name: Mayo Free Cabbage Salad

recipeInstructions.text: Whisk canola oil, sugar, red wine vinegar, and soy sauce together in a large bowl until sugar has dissolved. Toss in cabbage, green onions, almonds, and sunflower seeds. Cover bowl and refrigerate before serving, at least 1 hour; slaw tastes better when chilled overnight.

review.reviewBody: I made this following the receipe and it was really good! Ialso made a custom version for me. Insted of canola I used olive oil, low sodium soy sauce, splenda, omitted the almonds and sunflower seeds. I sprinkled with chow mein noodles and it was awesome. I like this more than the mayo version cole slaw!

Great and well received. I reduced the amount of sugar by half and increased the amount of cabbage because the bags held 12 oz. instead of 8. But there is more than enough dressing still. I put it in Tupperware and turn it upside down part of the time it is "marinating". Delicious!

Fast and easy and everyone asks for seconds. My changes: rice wine vinegar instead of red wine vinegar and I use part olive/part sesame oil to give it more flavor and Splenda or Truvia instead of sugar. Also, I saute the slivered almonds in butter to brown them and make them more crunchy. Can also add a package of ramen noodles (crushed) to pan and saute til brown for more crunch but we usually leave those out on our low carb diet. Either way, delish!

Used the only size bag of cabbage available, 16 oz. Kept the dressing ingredients pretty much the same, though I DID use only 4 1/2 tablespoons of sugar and used rice wine vinegar to use it up. As a personal preference for a CRISPY crunch instead of merely the crunch given by slivered almonds, I opted for chow mein noodles MIXED IN ONLY PRIOR TO SERVING to keep the integrity of the crispy crunch. Made in the a.m. for p.m. service. Delicious!

Absolutely loved the taste! However, two things stood out for us. First, The amount of dressing this makes is way too much for the amount of cabbage. I shredded my own and had about twice what the recipe called for, so I was going to double the dressing ingredients. At the last minute, I did not, and am glad---as is, it was still way too much. Second the ratio of oil to vinegar is too high. Too much oil in this dressing. I would think about 70/30 would be better. 30% oil and 70% other liquids.
I reduced the sugar to 2 tablespoons and replaced the canola with 1/3 cup light olive oil. I also added 1 tablespoon of sesame oil and topped with chow mein noodles. Excellent

So far this is my favorite no mayo slaw recipe and I make it regularly. Really good as written, but I prefer less oil and less sugar - I have the oil down to about 1/8 of a cup and the sugar down to 4 Tbsp. If it doesn't seem like enough liquid, I'll add more vinegar. These changes are only an attempt to make it healthier, not make it taste better. I usually use 1/2 large head of cabbage. Lately I've been using red cabbage, it looks more appealing than green cabbage - which turns a little brown from the soy. Have also substituted sweet or yellow onion for the green onions. The sunflower seeds give nice texture, we add them when serving so they don't get soggy and usually skip the almonds. The salad is good without seeds too. Also great as a sandwich topping. Wonder how this would be with some dried cranberries or cherries!

This dressing is phenomenal! I changed it only slightly: instead of all canola oil, I used half canola oil and the other half substituted an excellent lime-infused olive oil made locally (Lucero Olive Oil--highly recommend). I similarly substituted in some flavored balsamic in place of part of the red wine vinegar. Since the balsamic adds a lot of sweetness I cut way back to only 3 tbsp of sugar even though I doubled the recipe, and it was exactly sweet enough but not too sweet. I'm going to make another batch of this dressing and keep it on hand for other salads! Thanks for sharing this :)

This is an easy, delicious recipe that avoids the fattening ingredients. Like others I substituted olive oil for canola, added 1/8 tsp. sesame oil in the dressing and added chopped green onions, sesame seeds, and sliced almonds to the salad. We also added chopped chicken to make it as meal.

Another delicious salad! I'm on a quest to use all that is in our fridge. This was a great recipe to use up the half-head of cabbage. I also used up the last of the carrots by shredding them and adding them to the mix. I prepared this in the morning, adding the almonds and the sunflower seeds and served it at dinner time. I did replace the 6 TB of sugar with 4 TB of Stevia and it worked well for our tastes. This could easily become a main dish meal by adding grilled chicken or shrimp. I served this with 'Sweet and Spicy Grilled Shrimp' and 'Stuffed Pea Pods', both from AR. Thanks, Shalvie for sharing your recipe.

Followed other reviewers suggestions of less sugar and more slaw mixture and used olive oil. Everyone liked very much so was all eaten. I don’t think it would save too well. Next time I will monitor the amount of dressing to slaw even more. Delicious flavours.
Made this for the first time today for a cookout. It was a hit!
Loved this. The first time I thought it was too sweet. Second time I cut the sugar in half. Perfect. Also used avocado oil.what do you think about olive oil for this? Anyone?
Awesome, no seed oils (used avocado oil and didn't add nuts). Added chow me in noodles. Tastes great!
I’ve just mixed it together, but cut the sugar in half. Right now it still tastes too sweet for my liking, but I’ll see how it works out once it’s chilled for a couple of hours and has time to blend.

A tasty lower-calorie version of the delicious "ramen-noodle" Chinese cabbage salads. Super easy to make. It does make a lot of dressing, so possibly add more veggies to balance it out, or reduce the amount of vinegar/oil
Really tastes good
Delicious sweet no mayo cole slaw. Easy and healthy (I reduced the sugar) crisp and savory.
We loved it, but I did add crumbled bacon the first time. The second time I added the bacon and fresh cilantro. Yum. Thanks for a great recipe.!
Delicious. I added raisins, no nuts, and I ate the whole bowl.
